newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan electricity rates up more than 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan electricity rates up more than 50 pct.

text.p: Venezuelan electricity rates have risen more than 50 percent in residential areas, according to figures published in Official Gazette.
Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta had said Friday the government approved a new increase in electricity tariffs -- the third this year -- but gave no figures.
The increases, effective Oct 4, vary according to company and region, the official resolution showed. They form part of an agreement with International Monetary Fund signed in July.

For Electricidad de Caracas, the country's leading privately owned electric utility and Caracas stock exchange's benchmark, a 54-percent hike was authorized in the capital Caracas and surrounding residential areas. In most other Venezuelan cities, the rises averaged over 50 percent.
Venezuelan electricity companies had been asking for tariff increases for months to meet spiraling costs generated by an inflation running at a record 115 percent annual rate.
Electric utilities received rate increases in May and August, mainly to compensate for inflationary and exchange rate losses.
Electricity de Caracas, for example, was granted a 9.65 percent increase in August which followed a 28 percent hike in May but these were deemed insufficient by company executives.

Following the latest rise, Electric Industry Chamber (Caveinal) President Carlos Perez Mibelli told El Universal daily Sunday that there would probably be no other increase authorized by the National Electricity Commission (CREE) this year.
